1 --- 2 title: Migrating to Cache Components 3 nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components 4 description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js. 5 related: 6 title: Next Steps 7 description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled. 8 links: 9 - app/guides/instant-navigation 10 - app/getting-started/caching 11 - app/guides/preserving-ui-state 12 - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components 13 - app/guides/authentication-with-cache-components 14 - app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params 15 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents 16 --- 17 18 When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). 19 20 The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight. 21 22 ## Use the adoption skill (recommended) 23 24 The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-cache-components-adoption) skill drives this migration with a coding agent, one feature at a time, checking in at every feature boundary. It supports two modes: 25 26 - **Incremental.** Opens a single mechanical PR that opts every route out of validation, then ships each feature as a follow-up PR. This automates the [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) flow below. 27 - **Direct.** Adopts every route in place on one branch. 28 29 Install the skill: 30 31 ```bash filename="Terminal" 32 npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption 33 ``` 34 35 Then give the agent this prompt: 36 37 ```prompt 38 Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption skill. 39 ``` 40 41 ## Or migrate by hand 42 43 Migrating an existing app by hand follows a few steps, in order: 44 45 1. [Enable Cache Components](#enable-cache-components) in `next.config.ts`. 46 2. Decide your approach: convert every route now, or [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) by [opting routes out of validation](#opting-out-of-validation) first and converting one at a time. 47 3. [Follow the validation errors and insights](#following-validation) it surfaces, replacing each route segment config with its Cache Components equivalent and caching uncached data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). The per-key sections below cover each config and API. 48 49 Your existing `fetch` and `unstable_cache` caching keeps working as a separate layer, so let the insights and errors guide what to change. 50 51 Some surfaces have their own steps: 52 53 - For routes with dynamic params, follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. 54 - For metadata, follow the [`generateMetadata` and `generateViewport`](#generatemetadata-and-generateviewport) guidance. 55 56 The sections below cover each config and API and what to do with it under Cache Components. 57 58 ## Enable Cache Components 59 60 Cache Components requires Next.js 16. If you're on Next.js 15 or earlier, upgrade first by following the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16). Coming from an older version, work through the [upgrade guides](/docs/app/guides/upgrading) to reach 16 before continuing. 61 62 Then enable the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) flag in `next.config.ts`: 63 64 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 65 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 66 67 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 68 cacheComponents: true, 69 } 70 71 export default nextConfig 72 ``` 73 74 > **Good to know:** If you were using `experimental.dynamicIO` or `experimental.useCache`, `cacheComponents` replaces them. See the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). 75 76 After enabling the flag, route segments that still export `dynamic`, `revalidate`, or `fetchCache` will error. Start by replacing those configs. The sections below explain what to do for each one. 77 78 ## Opting out of validation 79 80 A validation insight or error tells you a route won't render instantly. Resolve it by following the recommendation: cache the data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrap it in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). If you're not ready to address it yet, set the [`instant`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) config to `false` on the segment that raised it (a layout, page, or parallel slot), then come back to it later. 81 82 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 83 export const instant = false 84 ``` 85 86 > **Good to know**: `instant = false` marks a segment as _allowed to block_. It does not force the route to be dynamic, so a genuinely prerenderable route still ships a static shell. It also does not clear synchronous IO build errors: calls like `new Date()`, `Math.random()`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` still fail the prerender. See [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally). 87 88 ## Adopting incrementally 89 90 You don't have to migrate every route at once. `instant = false` lets you get the whole app building and running first, then convert routes one at a time: 91 92 1. **Enable the flag and migrate each route segment config.** Follow the relevant sections below for [`dynamic = "force-dynamic"`](#dynamic--force-dynamic), [`dynamic = "force-static"`](#dynamic--force-static), [`revalidate`](#revalidate), and [`fetchCache`](#fetchcache). For routes with dynamic params, also follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. Routes that still render instantly need no further work. 93 2. **Opt out the routes that aren't ready.** Where an insight or error appears, set `instant = false` on the segment that raised it. To do this in one pass across the whole app, run the [`cache-components-instant-false`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#cache-components-instant-false) codemod, which adds the opt-out to every `page`, `layout`, and `default` that doesn't already declare `instant`: 94 95 ```bash filename="Terminal" 96 npx @next/codemod@canary cache-components-instant-false ./app 97 ``` 98 99 > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count. 100 101 The app keeps building and serving, now with validation deferred for the opted-out routes. 102 103 3. **Fix synchronous IO. It can't be deferred.** Calls like `new Date()`, `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` during prerender throw a build error that `instant = false` does not clear, so a route that uses them won't build until you address it, opt-out or not. Move the call out of the prerendered shell so it runs at request time: wrap the part that needs it in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) and call [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) before the call, or move it into a Client Component. 104 4. **Convert one route at a time.** Remove `instant = false` from a route, then resolve its insights by caching data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). Repeat until no routes opt out. 105 106 ## Following validation 107 108 Cache Components validates your routes in development and surfaces errors and insights in the dev overlay. Some look like this, naming the affected component and pointing at a fix: 109 110 111 ' }, 119 { text: '}' }, 120 ]} 121 /> 122 ', highlight: true }, 128 { text: ' ' }, 129 { text: '', highlight: true }, 130 ]} 131 /> 132 133 134 Each card is clickable and opens a page with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs. Work through the insights and errors until they're gone. For the full validation workflow, the DevTools, and CI testing, see the [instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation). 135 136 Insights don't show up in the HTTP response. An offending route still returns `200` with rendered HTML in dev. The insight only appears in the dev overlay, the dev-server log, or the [MCP `get_errors` tool](/docs/app/guides/mcp). To see them, read the overlay (or query the MCP). 137 138 ## `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` 139 140 **Not needed.** All pages are dynamic by default. 141 142 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 143 // Before - No longer needed 144 export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' 145 146 export default function Page() { 147 return
...
148 } 149 ``` 150 151 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 152 // Before - No longer needed 153 export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' 154 155 export default function Page() { 156 return
...
157 } 158 ``` 159 160 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 161 // After - Just remove it 162 export default function Page() { 163 return
...
164 } 165 ``` 166 167 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 168 // After - Just remove it 169 export default function Page() { 170 return
...
171 } 172 ``` 173 174 ## `dynamic = "force-static"` 175 176 Start by removing it. When unhandled uncached or runtime data access is detected during development and build time, Next.js raises an error. Otherwise, the prerendering step automatically extracts the static HTML shell. 177 178 For uncached data access, add [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) as close to the data access as possible with a long [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) like `'max'` to maintain cached behavior. If needed, add it at the top of the page or layout. 179 180 For runtime data access (`cookies()`, `headers()`, etc.), errors will direct you to wrap it with ``. Since you started by using `force-static`, you must remove the runtime data access to prevent any request time work. 181 182 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 183 // Before 184 export const dynamic = 'force-static' 185 186 export default async function Page() { 187 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 188 return
...
189 } 190 ``` 191 192 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 193 // Before 194 export const dynamic = 'force-static' 195 196 export default async function Page() { 197 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 198 return
...
199 } 200 ``` 201 202 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 203 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 204 205 // After - Use 'use cache' instead 206 export default async function Page() { 207 'use cache' 208 cacheLife('max') 209 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 210 return
...
211 } 212 ``` 213 214 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 215 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 216 217 // After - Use 'use cache' instead 218 export default async function Page() { 219 'use cache' 220 cacheLife('max') 221 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 222 return
...
223 } 224 ``` 225 226 ## `revalidate` 227 228 **Replace with `cacheLife`.** Use the `cacheLife` function to define cache duration instead of the route segment config. 229 230 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 231 // Before 232 export const revalidate = 3600 // 1 hour 233 234 export default async function Page() { 235 return
...
236 } 237 ``` 238 239 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 240 // Before 241 export const revalidate = 3600 // 1 hour 242 243 export default async function Page() { 244 return
...
245 } 246 ``` 247 248 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 249 // After - Use cacheLife 250 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 251 252 export default async function Page() { 253 'use cache' 254 cacheLife('hours') 255 return
...
256 } 257 ``` 258 259 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 260 // After - Use cacheLife 261 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 262 263 export default async function Page() { 264 'use cache' 265 cacheLife('hours') 266 return
...
267 } 268 ``` 269 270 > **Good to know**: If your `revalidate` value doesn't match a built-in [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) profile (`'seconds'`, `'minutes'`, `'hours'`, `'days'`, `'weeks'`, `'max'`), pick the closest one or define a [custom profile](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#custom-cache-profiles) to match your conventions. You can also [redefine a built-in profile](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#overriding-the-default-cache-profiles), including `default`, when its timings don't match your application's caching needs. 271 272 ## `fetchCache` 273 274 **Not needed.** With `use cache`, all data fetching within a cached scope is automatically cached, making `fetchCache` unnecessary. 275 276 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 277 // Before 278 export const fetchCache = 'force-cache' 279 ``` 280 281 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 282 // Before 283 export const fetchCache = 'force-cache' 284 ``` 285 286 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 287 // After - Use 'use cache' to control caching behavior 288 export default async function Page() { 289 'use cache' 290 // All fetches here are cached 291 return
...
292 } 293 ``` 294 295 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 296 // After - Use 'use cache' to control caching behavior 297 export default async function Page() { 298 'use cache' 299 // All fetches here are cached 300 return
...
301 } 302 ``` 303 304 ## `fetch` cache options 305 306 **Move `cache` and `next` options to `use cache`.** 307 308 Without Cache Components, you cache a request with `cache: 'force-cache'` and tune it with `next: { revalidate, tags }`. 309 310 With Cache Components, wrap the fetch in a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) function. Fetches inside that scope are cached automatically, and `revalidate` and `tags` become [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag). 311 312 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 313 // Before 314 export default async function Page() { 315 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data', { 316 cache: 'force-cache', 317 next: { revalidate: 3600, tags: ['data'] }, 318 }) 319 const data = await res.json() 320 return
...
321 } 322 ``` 323 324 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 325 // Before 326 export default async function Page() { 327 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data', { 328 cache: 'force-cache', 329 next: { revalidate: 3600, tags: ['data'] }, 330 }) 331 const data = await res.json() 332 return
...
333 } 334 ``` 335 336 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 337 // After 338 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 339 340 async function getData() { 341 'use cache' 342 cacheLife('hours') 343 cacheTag('data') 344 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 345 return res.json() 346 } 347 348 export default async function Page() { 349 const data = await getData() 350 return
...
351 } 352 ``` 353 354 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 355 // After 356 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 357 358 async function getData() { 359 'use cache' 360 cacheLife('hours') 361 cacheTag('data') 362 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 363 return res.json() 364 } 365 366 export default async function Page() { 367 const data = await getData() 368 return
...
369 } 370 ``` 371 372 Note the persistence difference. The `fetch` Data Cache persists cached responses across deployments and across serverless instances. 373 374 `use cache` defaults to in-memory storage, so its entries are discarded when the serverless instance is destroyed and are scoped to a single deployment. Use [`use cache: remote`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) or a [cache handler](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers) for storage that survives instance teardown. Even with durable storage, expect cached values to recompute after a new deployment. 375 376 ## `unstable_cache` 377 378 **Replace with `use cache`.** 379 380 `unstable_cache` is replaced by the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. 381 382 Turn the wrapped function into a function with the `'use cache'` directive. The cache key is derived automatically from the arguments, so the key-parts array is no longer needed, and the `options` object maps to [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag). 383 384 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 385 // Before 386 import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache' 387 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 388 389 export const getUser = unstable_cache( 390 async (id: string) => { 391 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 392 }, 393 ['user'], // cache key prefix 394 { tags: ['users'], revalidate: 3600 } 395 ) 396 ``` 397 398 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 399 // Before 400 import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache' 401 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 402 403 export const getUser = unstable_cache( 404 async (id) => { 405 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 406 }, 407 ['user'], // cache key prefix 408 { tags: ['users'], revalidate: 3600 } 409 ) 410 ``` 411 412 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 413 // After 414 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 415 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 416 417 export async function getUser(id: string) { 418 'use cache' 419 cacheLife('hours') 420 cacheTag('users') 421 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 422 } 423 ``` 424 425 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 426 // After 427 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 428 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 429 430 export async function getUser(id) { 431 'use cache' 432 cacheLife('hours') 433 cacheTag('users') 434 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 435 } 436 ``` 437 438 Like the `fetch` Data Cache, `unstable_cache` persists cached values across deployments and serverless instances, while `use cache` does not. See [`fetch` cache options](#fetch-cache-options) above for the storage details. 439 440 ## `React.cache` 441 442 **Usually no change.** `React.cache` continues to deduplicate matching calls within a React render. 443 444 However, each Cache Function has an isolated React cache scope. Calls from separate Cache Functions do not share a `React.cache` result, such as when one Cache Function preloads data and another consumes it. 445 446 When a helper reads request data and matching calls need to share work across Cache Function scopes, replace the React wrapper with [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). If the function only needs request-scoped deduplication, use `cacheLife({ stale: Infinity })` so it does not lower the route's stale time. Private Cache Function results are not stored in a server cache across production requests. 447 448 ## On-demand revalidation (`revalidateTag`, `revalidatePath`, `updateTag`) 449 450 On-demand invalidation still works by tagging cached data and expiring it after an event. Tag data with [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) inside a `use cache` function instead of the `fetch` `next.tags` option, then choose the invalidation API by the behavior you want: 451 452 - [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag): for mutations whose result the user must see immediately (read-your-own-writes). Called from a Server Action, it expires the tag so the next request waits for fresh data instead of serving stale content. 453 - [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag): for stale-while-revalidate. A cache profile is **required** as the second argument, for example use `'max'` to serve cached data while it refreshes in the background. Works in Server Actions and Route Handlers. 454 - [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath): unchanged from the previous caching model. 455 456 `updateTag` isn't exclusive to Cache Components (it also works with the previous caching model), but migrating is a good time to adopt it. After a mutation in a Server Action, reach for it when the user should see their own change right away. 457 458 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 459 'use server' 460 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 461 462 export async function createPost(formData: FormData) { 463 // Create the post, then show it immediately on the next request 464 updateTag('posts') 465 } 466 ``` 467 468 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 469 'use server' 470 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 471 472 export async function createPost(formData) { 473 // Create the post, then show it immediately on the next request 474 updateTag('posts') 475 } 476 ``` 477 478 > **Good to know:** `updateTag` can only be called from a Server Action; calling it elsewhere throws. In Route Handlers or webhooks, use `revalidateTag` instead with a cache profile. 479 480 Pass `'max'` as the second argument to `revalidateTag` to expire the tag with stale-while-revalidate semantics: 481 482 ```tsx filename="app/api/webhook/route.ts" switcher 483 // Before 484 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 485 486 export async function POST() { 487 revalidateTag('posts') 488 return Response.json({ ok: true }) 489 } 490 ``` 491 492 ```js filename="app/api/webhook/route.js" switcher 493 // Before 494 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 495 496 export async function POST() { 497 revalidateTag('posts') 498 return Response.json({ ok: true }) 499 } 500 ``` 501 502 ```tsx filename="app/api/webhook/route.ts" switcher 503 // After - Pass a cache profile 504 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 505 506 export async function POST() { 507 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 508 return Response.json({ ok: true }) 509 } 510 ``` 511 512 ```js filename="app/api/webhook/route.js" switcher 513 // After - Pass a cache profile 514 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 515 516 export async function POST() { 517 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 518 return Response.json({ ok: true }) 519 } 520 ``` 521 522 ## `unstable_noStore` 523 524 **Not needed.** `unstable_noStore` (`noStore()`) opts a component out of caching. } ``` The profile name tells Next.js how to cache the entire function's output. If you don't call `cacheLife`, the `default` profile is used.
